title: "Comping rhythm: So What: the answer"

This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **So What: the answer**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read the band's last four bars on the staff underneath. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd) · [Comping rhythms](index.qmd#chords)

## The pattern

A two-bar pattern. Nothing in the first bar, under the bass call. In the second, two chords: the voicing a whole step above the chord, held from beat 3, then the chord itself, short, on the and of 4. Use the Fourths voicing for the sound of the record.

It belongs in *Swing*. Here it is in the swing style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|Dm7|Dm7|Dm7|Ebm7|Ebm7|Dm7|Dm7" data-tempo="132" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"So What: the answer","opts":{"compRhythm":"sowhat"}}]'></div>

## Step 1: Long notes

Start with something simpler. One held chord per bar (or per chord). Leaves the most room for a soloist.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords-pad.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|Dm7|Dm7|Dm7|Ebm7|Ebm7|Dm7|Dm7" data-tempo="92" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Long notes","opts":{"compRhythm":"pad"}}]'></div>

## Step 2: Off-beats

Chords on the and of 1 and the and of 3, never on a downbeat.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords-offbeats.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|Dm7|Dm7|Dm7|Ebm7|Ebm7|Dm7|Dm7" data-tempo="92" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Off-beats","opts":{"compRhythm":"offbeats"}}]'></div>

## Step 3: So What: the answer, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Two bars: nothing in the first while the bass plays the call; in the second, a chord a whole step above held from 3, then the chord itself, short, on the and of 4. 'So what.'

The band plays it on piano here; the step after next has it on guitar.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|Dm7|Dm7|Dm7|Ebm7|Ebm7|Dm7|Dm7" data-tempo="92" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"So What: the answer","opts":{"compRhythm":"sowhat"}},{"label":"Off-beats (the step before)","opts":{"compRhythm":"offbeats"}}]'></div>

## Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 132 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's chord player off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|Dm7|Dm7|Dm7|Ebm7|Ebm7|Dm7|Dm7" data-tempo="132" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"So What: the answer","opts":{"compRhythm":"sowhat"}}]'></div>

## Step 5: On the guitar

The same rhythm on the guitar. On guitar each chord is a strum or a pluck of a chord shape; a short chord is choked by easing the fretting hand off the strings.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|Dm7|Dm7|Dm7|Ebm7|Ebm7|Dm7|Dm7" data-tempo="132" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"So What: the answer","opts":{"compRhythm":"sowhat"}}]'></div>

## Step 6: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. The pattern keeps its rhythm and changes chord where the bar does: watch the staff for the hit that lands on beat 3.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7 G7|Em7 A7|Dm7 G7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="132" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"So What: the answer","opts":{"compRhythm":"sowhat"}}]'></div>
